data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The distinction between truly independent failures and failures appearing uncorrelated is uniquely identifiable through the 'Recovery Signature' (temporal and spatial distribution of recovery) rather than the 'Failure Signature'.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The recovery process itself is gated by a shared dependency (e.g., a global DNS provider), making independent failures appear correlated during the recovery phase.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The 'noise' of high-frequency independent failures masks the signal of the recovery wave.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Independent failures occur and resolve according to local conditions; conversely, failures caused by a shared hidden trigger (e.g., a global network event or a specific BGP route leak) will exhibit a synchronized recovery wave, where disparate services return to health within a tight temporal window despite failing at staggered intervals.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
